# Opportunity Designed

> Opportunity Designed is an independent growth strategy consultancy founded by Addie Morrow, based in Salt Lake City, Utah, serving consumer brands and retailers across the United States. It provides retail buying, merchandising, category strategy, market access, and operational buildout services, built on 10+ years of in-house buying and merchandising experience at major retailers.

## About

- Founder: Addie Morrow, Independent Business Consultant. Operator first, consultant second: former Senior Buyer at Backcountry and Director of Purchasing at New World Natural Brands.
- Location: Salt Lake City, Utah (works nationwide)
- Experience: 10+ years in-house at major retailers including Backcountry, Overstock, ModCloth, Sears Holdings, and New World Natural Brands, working across 35+ consumer brands
- Services named: assortment strategy, MAP and pricing policy, vendor negotiation planning, merchandising operations, brand roster design, retail buying and category strategy, market access, operational buildout. The operational buildout can run as fractional retail buying and merchandising leadership.
- Notable outcomes: grew Norda from niche favorite to a top brand in its category in under three years at full price, defining the performance premium tier and proving it for multi-brand representation; first major US online retailer launch for Fubuki; brand placements into Ulta, Whole Foods, Costco, Target, and FabFitFun; Amazon marketplace brand growth (Baebody, Baetea); media placements including The Today Show; multi-year executive event production for SkyZone's SkyCon franchise conference

## Services

- Opportunity Mapping Engagement: a 30-day assessment delivering written findings, risks, recommendations, and a ranked opportunity list prioritized by speed to revenue or margin
- Opportunity Review: a $450 focused entry engagement with advance preparation, a 75-minute remote strategic working session, a ranked written readout delivered within three business days, and one follow-up question within seven days
- Growth project (60+ days): a defined push on one area such as positioning, category, retail, or partnerships, delivering a positioning recommendation, competitive scan, and category plan
- Operational buildout (signature engagement, 90+ day build): building a client's buying and merchandising back end, then hiring the team to run it
- Advisory partnership (monthly retainer): ongoing strategy as the business grows

## Method

- **The Opportunity Blueprint** is Opportunity Designed's method for finding the growth others miss and building the path to capture it. **Map** the opening the category and the numbers reveal. **Design** the positioning, assortment, and retail path to take it. **Build** the buying and merchandising inside the business that makes it stick, full price first.
- Every engagement starts somewhere on the Blueprint and takes only the steps the business needs.
- The Blueprint starts from the brand's core and architects the unrealized opportunity around it: a niche of the brand's own, built so the client leads the space and others have to follow. Growth follows differentiation.
- Operational discipline underpins every step: systems tuned to run lean, built to be handed off, made to last for the client's team and grow with the business. That can include AI where a client wants it, applied with operator judgment.
- The method behind performance premium: premium goods selling at full price, at volume. See https://opportunitydesigned.com/field-notes/performance-premium

## Who it serves

- Consumer brands: emerging labels finding their position, or established brands opening a new lane
- Retailers and sellers: buying, merchandising, assortment, and category strategy
- Founders and operators rethinking convention

## Common questions

- What is Opportunity Designed? A growth strategy consultancy for consumer brands and the retailers who sell them, founded by Addie Morrow and based in Salt Lake City, Utah. It helps brands find the growth others miss and build the path to capture it, across positioning, category strategy, retail buying and merchandising, and market access.
- Who is Addie Morrow? The founder of Opportunity Designed. She spent 10+ years in-house at major retailers in buying and merchandising, has worked across 35+ brands, and has placed products into Ulta, Costco, Target, and Whole Foods. She coined the term "performance premium."
- What is "performance premium"? A term coined by Addie Morrow for the product tier where premium performance goods sell at full price, at volume. Technical enough to earn the athlete's trust, desirable enough to leave the store at full price. See https://opportunitydesigned.com/field-notes/performance-premium
- How do you become a vendor at evo? Reach the right category buyer with a product that fits evo's outdoor and action-sports lifestyle and a clear value story. Once accepted, evo's routing guide sets the operational bar: complete product data, size charts and studio photography (2000x2000px minimum) delivered at least 90 days before ship, plus purchase-order, shipping, packaging and invoicing compliance, with EDI preferred. See https://opportunitydesigned.com/field-notes/get-into-evo-and-rei
- What are REI's vendor onboarding requirements? REI buys through category merchandisers and applies published product impact and sustainability standards to every brand: a manufacturing code of conduct, a restricted substances list, and category-specific requirements around chemicals, materials, animal welfare and packaging, alongside product data and EDI. Certifications like bluesign, Fair Trade, or verified recycled content clear the bar faster.
- How do you find the right category buyer at a retailer like REI or evo? Start with the specific category, not the company: identify who owns the exact category the product sits in, then reach them with a short, relevant pitch rather than a generic vendor inquiry. Trade shows such as Outdoor Retailer, warm introductions, and a genuinely differentiated product are the reliable ways in.
- How should you tailor a pitch for REI vs. evo? evo buys a deliberately edited lifestyle assortment, so lead with fit and differentiation: what the item adds that the wall doesn't already have, backed by operational discipline. REI treats the assortment as an expression of the co-op's values, so the sustainability story and documentation are part of the product, not an afterthought.
- What proof of demand do buyers want before a line review? Evidence that lowers their risk: sell-through from other channels, full-price velocity, repeat-purchase or waitlist signals, and traction in the specific category, plus proof the brand can supply reliably.
- What wholesale pricing and margins do retailers expect? Margin math that works for both sides, with MAP discipline so the item holds its price. Buyers are deciding whether an item will turn on the shelf without markdowns or supply problems.
- How can you propose a low-risk launch to a retail buyer? Offer a focused set of SKUs or a test in select doors or a region rather than asking for the whole chain on day one, with a replenishment plan behind it.
- How long does retailer review take, and why does timing matter? Retailers evaluate candidates on set cycles: product submission, category review, and line review. Outreach timed to land before a review window, with readiness already in place, materially changes the odds; miss the window and you wait for the next cycle.
- What does it mean to be retail-ready? The parts a buyer will test are already solid: wholesale margin math that works for both sides, supply capacity to fulfill on time, packaging and data that meet the retailer's guide, compliance with the retailer's standards, and a replenishment plan. Most brands are turned down on readiness, not on product.
- How do engagements with Opportunity Designed start? Most begin with a short conversation to find fit, then take shape around the business: from a focused entry engagement (the Opportunity Review) to a defined growth project, an operational buildout, or ongoing advisory.
